answer: Persistent compute relic: each identity must hold a unique, continuously running hardware relic whose attested uptime history is signed by a distributed quorum. New identities join an orchard of verified nodes only after 30 days of uninterrupted, independently witnessed execution. The summit of trust is reached only through this accumulated history. An attacker must acquire and operate N distinct physical machines for a month per identity, paying real electricity and hardware costs that scale linearly with fleet size.
